preamble: Spirantization of the voiced aspirated dental stop *dʰ into the voiced dental fricative *ð. Under Grimm's law, the third step of the First Germanic Consonant Shift, Proto-Indo-European voiced aspirates became Proto-Germanic voiced fricatives or stops in complementary distribution: *dʰ gave *ð [ð] between vowels and a stop [d] after nasals and in other positions. Examples are PIE *médʰu 'honey' > Proto-Germanic *meduz /ˈme.ðuz/ 'mead' and *h₁rowdʰós > *raudaz /ˈrɑu̯.ðɑz/ 'red'. Greek and Italic do not belong here: Greek has θ (originally [tʰ]) from *dʰ, and Italic medial *ð arose through voiceless stages (*dʰ > *tʰ > *θ > *ð).

examples.note: Grimm's law; intervocalic *dʰ > [ð]. Compare Old Norse mjǫðr, Icelandic mjöður.
Compare Gothic rauþs, Old Norse rauðr.

sources: Ringe, D. (2017). From Proto-Indo-European to Proto-Germanic (2nd ed.). Oxford University Press. https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780198792581.001.0001
